title: Adjustment Disorder - Rule-outs and Discriminators
content:
DOCUMENT TYPE: Differential

CORE ALIASES: Adjustment disorder with depressed mood, with anxiety, with mixed anxiety and depressed mood, with disturbance of conduct.

RULE-OUTS / DIFFERENTIALS:
- Major Depressive Disorder: If full MDD criteria are met (5+ symptoms including depressed mood or anhedonia for 2 weeks), diagnose MDD, not adjustment disorder. Episodic rather than purely reactive.
- PTSD / Acute Stress Disorder: Requires exposure to actual or threatened death, serious injury, or sexual violence. Adjustment disorder stressors are typically non-traumatic (job loss, divorce, move, illness).
- Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Worry is excessive, pervasive, and not clearly linked to one recent identifiable stressor.
- Normal bereavement: Sadness after death of loved one without marked impairment or prolonged duration beyond cultural norms.
- Substance/Medication-Induced: Symptoms attributable to intoxication or withdrawal.

COUNTER-SIGNALS / NEGATIONS: "No history of mania", "symptoms started right after the breakup", "not like my usual self", "this is new since the layoff", "I was fine before the move". Absence of flashbacks, hypervigilance, or trauma re-experiencing argues against PTSD. Lack of pervasive worry across unrelated domains argues against GAD.

PATIENT-LANGUAGE EXAMPLES: "Ever since I lost the job everything feels overwhelming", "I can't stop crying since the diagnosis", "My sleep is wrecked because of the custody battle".

PROVENANCE: DSM-5-TR. Clinical consensus: Distinguish by proportionality to stressor and time course.
